OLED_MODEL_DOC: Controller and model, as reported by 'mpd_oled -o help'. For a 128x64 SSD1306 try SSD1306,128X64_NONAME first, then SSD1306,128X64 or SSD1306,128X64_ALT0. Many panels sold as SSD1306 are in fact SH1106, so SH1106,128X64_NONAME is also worth trying.
XOFFSET_DOC: Shifts the image right by this many pixels. Increase it if the first character on a line is clipped at the left edge. This happens when the panel's visible area starts partway into the controller's memory, which varies between panels sold under the same name. Try 1, 2 and 3.
I2C_ADDRESS_DOC: Leave empty for the default of 3c. Set to 3d if your panel uses the alternate address.
ROTATE_DOC: Turn the image upside down, for a panel mounted inverted.
CH341_INDEX_DOC: Which CH341A to use when more than one is plugged in. 0 is the first found.
CH341_SPEED_DOC: 400 kHz gives roughly three times the frame rate of 100 kHz and is the default. Reduce it if long leads or weak pull-up resistors make the display unreliable.
FRAMERATE_DOC: Requested frames per second. The USB adapter limits full-screen redraws to roughly 26 per second at 400 kHz, so higher values have no effect.
SPECTRUM_DOC: Show the audio spectrum. The audio tap stays in the chain while the plugin is enabled so Mixer Type Software, None and Hardware keep a stable path. Turn this off to leave the bars blank.
SPECTRUM_DELAY_DOC: Delays the bars to match the sound. The spectrum is measured before the audio output buffer, so the bars can run ahead of what you hear by however much that buffer holds. How far ahead depends on your output device, so start at 0 and increase in steps of 100 until the bars land on the beat. A typical value is between 300 and 700.
SPECTRUM_SENSITIVITY_DOC: How tall the bars are for a given signal level. Raise it if the bars are always small, lower it if they reach the top on ordinary material. 100 is the starting point. Set it to 0 to let the analyser adjust itself instead, which is not recommended here: the audio is measured before the volume control, so its level never varies and there is nothing for automatic adjustment to follow except the silence between tracks. It raises the gain during a quiet gap and then cuts it back when the music returns, which shows as the bars filling the display for a few seconds after every pause. A fixed value also means a quiet passage looks quiet, rather than being amplified to fill the display.
